subject: handoff from quivive-qeg (high confidence)
body:
Inherited from quivive-qeg, closed by skeleton.
Confidence: high — verified: tested, reproduced, or read from the source

Crate/binary is now `quivive` (target/debug/quivive); CLI surface is exactly tile|watch|why, no completion. main.rs and lib.rs own ALL command wiring and module declarations (pub mod registry/stream/watch/why in lib.rs) -- do not edit main.rs or lib.rs, only your own module. Stub signatures to build against: registry::run() -> Result<()>, watch::run() -> Result<()>, why::run(repo: &Path, json: bool) -> Result<()>, stream::run(common: &cli::Common) -> Result<()>; each currently bails "not implemented yet (bead <id>)" (registry=quivive-113, stream=quivive-5uv, watch=quivive-8mq, why=quivive-15r), which main.rs propagates via `?` to exit 1 -- no special-casing needed when you implement it, just stop returning Err. `quivive why <repo> [--json]` and `quivive tile --stream` are wired as real subcommands/flags already; `tile`'s other flags (--repo/--json/windows/--exit-on/--no-cursor) are unchanged. The old interval-loop `watch --interval` is gone entirely -- S14's watch fires on transitions, not a timer, so quivive-8mq designs its own flags on Command::Watch (currently a bare unit variant) in cli.rs, which future beads MAY edit (only main.rs/lib.rs are frozen). VIGIL_NOW env seam is renamed QUIVIVE_NOW everywhere in src/lib.rs and tests. One loose end for quivive-113 or whoever touches cursor.rs next: the resume-cursor filename constant (src/cursor.rs::CURSOR_FILE) is still literally "vigil-cursor.json" -- untouched because cursor.rs was out of this bead's lease scope, and cli.rs's --no-cursor help text was kept accurate to that fact rather than renamed to match the binary.

subject: handoff from quivive-113 (high confidence)
body:
Inherited from quivive-113, closed by registry.
Confidence: high — verified: tested, reproduced, or read from the source

Public surface: pub fn registry::read() -> anyhow::Result<Vec<PathBuf>> (no args) — the old stubbed run() -> Result<()> was unused anywhere in the codebase (grepped: nothing called it) so I replaced it outright rather than layering a second function; there is no CLI subcommand for the registry (S2) so nothing else needed to change shape. Also exposed pub fn registry_path() -> Result<PathBuf> for callers/diagnostics that want the resolved path without reading it. Behavior: reads $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/quivive/repos, else ~/.config/quivive/repos; blank lines and lines whose first non-blank char is # are skipped (inline # is NOT a comment — paths may legally contain one); a leading ~ or ~/... expands against $HOME (no ~user); missing file -> Ok(vec![]), not an error; any other read error -> Err naming the path. DEDUPE RULE: entries are deduped on the post-expansion path, keeping first-occurrence order — two registry lines naming the same repo (even if one uses ~ and the other doesn't) tick it once. No validation that an entry is a real/live directory — that's explicitly left to the tick's per-repo degradation, documented in the module doc comment. Commit e0156db on agent/registry, all gates (fmt/clippy -D warnings/test) green.

subject: handoff from quivive-ykn (high confidence)
body:
Inherited from quivive-ykn, closed by state.
Confidence: high — verified: tested, reproduced, or read from the source

The seam is in src/state.rs (commit d96a39d), after the existing State/Thresholds
machine, before its #[cfg(test)] block. It touches nothing else.

CONSTRUCTION (readers build this, no logic needed):
- RepoSnapshot { agents: BTreeMap<String, DateTime<Utc>>, leases: Vec<LeaseSnapshot>,
  plan: Option<PlanSnapshot>, needs_decision: Vec<String>, pact_present: bool,
  degraded: Vec<String> } — "everything one tick learned about one repo," Default
  derived so partial construction is `RepoSnapshot { field: val, ..Default::default() }`.
  `agents` is the SAME TYPE as reader::Readings::agents (BTreeMap<String, DateTime<Utc>>) —
  no conversion needed, just move/clone it in. `leases` is LeaseSnapshot (agent, path,
  acquired_at, expires_at), a deliberate MIRROR of reader::lease::Lease rather than an
  import — state.rs must not depend on reader (keeps the pure-judgment layer free of
  reader's file-I/O/serde concerns; reader depends on nothing in state today and this
  keeps that a straight line, not a cycle). `plan` is a mirror of .pact/plan.json narrowed
  to S18's needs: PlanSnapshot { waves: Vec<WaveSnapshot> }, WaveSnapshot { wave: u32,
  gates: Vec<GateSnapshot>, started: Vec<String> } (started = bead/task ids the events
  tail shows as begun in that wave), GateSnapshot { id: String, closed: bool }. No plan
  reader exists yet anywhere in the tree — quivive-15r (why) or quivive-eea (tile) is
  probably where .pact/plan.json actually gets parsed into this shape; state.rs only
  defines what a parser must produce. `needs_decision` is bead ids straight from the
  sidecar, already filtered — filtering the sidecar's own shape is the sidecar reader's
  job, not this file's.

DERIVATION:
- `assess(snapshot: &RepoSnapshot, now: DateTime<Utc>, thresholds: &Thresholds) -> RepoAssessment`
  is the one entry point. RepoAssessment { agents: BTreeMap<String, State>, status:
  RepoStatus, attention: Vec<AttentionItem> } (attention sorted, deterministic order).
- RepoStatus (S8, five variants: HumanNeeded, Active, Drained, AllQuiet, NoFleet) derives
  Serialize with #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")] so it emits exactly S8's spellings
  (human-needed, active, drained, all-quiet, no-fleet) with zero extra code on your side.
  Precedence is one if/else chain in derive_status: attention non-empty -> HumanNeeded;
  else any agent Active/Idle -> Active; else (plan.is_some() || agents non-empty) ->
  Drained; else pact_present -> AllQuiet; else NoFleet. Total — always returns exactly one
  variant, proptest-by-hand in status_precedence_is_total_over_every_combination covers it.
- AttentionItem (S16-S18, three variants) derives Serialize with #[serde(tag = "kind",
  rename_all = "snake_case")] — JSON shape is {"kind": "dead_holding_paths", "agent":
  ..., "paths": [...], "remaining_ttl": ...} etc. That tagging is MY default choice, not
  dictated by docs/tile-contract.md (which doesn't cover attention items yet) — quivive-eea
  should treat it as a starting point and adjust if the actual tile JSON needs something
  else, updating tile-contract.md when it does.
  * DeadHoldingPaths { agent, paths (sorted), remaining_ttl } — one item per dead-or-
    unknown holder, not one per lease; remaining_ttl is the MINIMUM remaining TTL across
    that holder's leases, clamped at 0 (never negative). A holder with a lease but no
    entry in `agents` is treated as dead (mirrors tile::Tile::build's blocked_leases logic).
  * NeedsDecision { bead_id } — one per snapshot.needs_decision entry, verbatim.
  * GateOrderViolation { started_id, started_wave, open_gate_id, gate_wave } — only the
    EARLIEST open gate blocking a given started_id is reported, not every open gate behind
    it, so closing gates one at a time doesn't reshuffle and refire the violation set.
- FleetDrained (S19) is deliberately NOT an AttentionItem and does not affect
  RepoStatus::HumanNeeded, even though S8's own prose cites "S16-S19" for human-needed —
  see the doc comment on derive_status for the full reasoning: S19 is defined as "status
  became Drained", a transition, not a level; folding it into `attention` would make the
  RepoStatus::Drained arm unreachable, which contradicts S8's own fifth line. It only
  exists on TransitionEvent.

TRANSITIONS (how watch/quivive-8mq should call this):
- `transitions(prev: &RepoAssessment, now: &RepoAssessment) -> Vec<TransitionEvent>`.
  TransitionEvent is Attention(AttentionItem) | FleetDrained — four total shapes, matching
  S16-S19 exactly. Call once per tick per repo: keep the PREVIOUS tick's RepoAssessment
  around (not the previous tile, not raw evidence), assess() the current tick, diff the
  two. Becoming-true-only is handled entirely inside transitions() via AttentionItem's
  private `identity()` method, which compares (kind, primary id[, secondary id]) and
  DELIBERATELY IGNORES remaining_ttl/started_wave/gate_wave-adjacent noise fields — do not
  compare AttentionItem payloads by full equality across ticks, or a dead-holding-paths
  item's counting-down TTL will look "new" every tick and spam notifications. FleetDrained
  fires off status transitioning INTO Drained specifically (prev != Drained, now ==
  Drained), not off any attention-item delta.
- Notification payload -> S20 follow-up command mapping (watch's job to format, not this
  file's): DeadHoldingPaths -> `pact lease ls`; NeedsDecision{bead_id} -> `bd show
  <bead_id>`; GateOrderViolation -> likely `recount explain --event-line N` but this file's
  payload has no event-line number — if S20 needs one for gate violations specifically,
  that's a gap to fill in the plan/events reader that builds PlanSnapshot, not in state.rs.

TESTING NOTES: RepoSnapshot/PlanSnapshot derive Default, so tests build minimal snapshots
via `RepoSnapshot { field: val, ..Default::default() }` — clippy's field_reassign_with_default
lint rejects `let mut s = X::default(); s.field = val;`, use the struct-update form instead.

  Serialize with #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")] so it emits exactly S8's spellings
  (human-needed, active, drained, all-quiet, no-fleet) with zero extra code on your side.
  Precedence is one if/else chain in derive_status: attention non-empty -> HumanNeeded;
  else any agent Active/Idle -> Active; else (plan.is_some() || agents non-empty) ->
  Drained; else pact_present -> AllQuiet; else NoFleet. Total — always returns exactly one
  variant, proptest-by-hand in status_precedence_is_total_over_every_combination covers it.
- AttentionItem (S16-S18, three variants) derives Serialize with #[serde(tag = "kind",
  rename_all = "snake_case")] — JSON shape is {"kind": "dead_holding_paths", "agent":
  ..., "paths": [...], "remaining_ttl": ...} etc. That tagging is MY default choice, not
  dictated by docs/tile-contract.md (which doesn't cover attention items yet) — quivive-eea
  should treat it as a starting point and adjust if the actual tile JSON needs something
  else, updating tile-contract.md when it does.
  * DeadHoldingPaths { agent, paths (sorted), remaining_ttl } — one item per dead-or-
    unknown holder, not one per lease; remaining_ttl is the MINIMUM remaining TTL across
    that holder's leases, clamped at 0 (never negative). A holder with a lease but no
    entry in `agents` is treated as dead (mirrors tile::Tile::build's blocked_leases logic).
  * NeedsDecision { bead_id } — one per snapshot.needs_decision entry, verbatim.
  * GateOrderViolation { started_id, started_wave, open_gate_id, gate_wave } — only the
    EARLIEST open gate blocking a given started_id is reported, not every open gate behind
    it, so closing gates one at a time doesn't reshuffle and refire the violation set.
- FleetDrained (S19) is deliberately NOT an AttentionItem and does not affect
  RepoStatus::HumanNeeded, even though S8's own prose cites "S16-S19" for human-needed —
  see the doc comment on derive_status for the full reasoning: S19 is defined as "status
  became Drained", a transition, not a level; folding it into `attention` would make the
  RepoStatus::Drained arm unreachable, which contradicts S8's own fifth line. It only
  exists on TransitionEvent.

TRANSITIONS (how watch/quivive-8mq should call this):
- `transitions(prev: &RepoAssessment, now: &RepoAssessment) -> Vec<TransitionEvent>`.
  TransitionEvent is Attention(AttentionItem) | FleetDrained — four total shapes, matching
  S16-S19 exactly. Call once per tick per repo: keep the PREVIOUS tick's RepoAssessment
  around (not the previous tile, not raw evidence), assess() the current tick, diff the
  two. Becoming-true-only is handled entirely inside transitions() via AttentionItem's
  private `identity()` method, which compares (kind, primary id[, secondary id]) and
  DELIBERATELY IGNORES remaining_ttl/started_wave/gate_wave-adjacent noise fields — do not
  compare AttentionItem payloads by full equality across ticks, or a dead-holding-paths
  item's counting-down TTL will look "new" every tick and spam notifications. FleetDrained
  fires off status transitioning INTO Drained specifically (prev != Drained, now ==
  Drained), not off any attention-item delta.
- Notification payload -> S20 follow-up command mapping (watch's job to format, not this
  file's): DeadHoldingPaths -> `pact lease ls`; NeedsDecision{bead_id} -> `bd show
  <bead_id>`; GateOrderViolation -> likely `recount explain --event-line N` but this file's
  payload has no event-line number — if S20 needs one for gate violations specifically,
  that's a gap to fill in the plan/events reader that builds PlanSnapshot, not in state.rs.

TESTING NOTES: RepoSnapshot/PlanSnapshot derive Default, so tests build minimal snapshots
via `RepoSnapshot { field: val, ..Default::default() }` — clippy's field_reassign_with_default
lint rejects `let mut s = X::default(); s.field = val;`, use the struct-update form instead.
